div.head: Duns Prol.
div.ab: Hoc est consilium, quod Anglie sapientes et plebis Walie consiliarii inter Dunsetas habuerunt.
Ðis is seo gerædnes, ðe Angelcynnes witan ⁊ Wealhðeode rædboran betweox Dunsetan gesetton.
This is the agreement that the English and Welsh counsellors established among the [people of ] Dunsæte.
Dies ist der Beschluss, den Englands Witan [einerseits] und die [regirenden] Staatsmänner des Walliser Volkes [andererseits, als Recht] zwischen den ‘Dunsæte’, festgesetzt haben.
This is the decree which England's witan [on the one side] and the [governing] statesmen of the Welsh people [on the other] have established [as law] among the ‘Dunsæte’.
div.note: The Latin is the Quadripartitus; Liebermann's Old English is from B (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 383, p. 93, c. 1125), and is the same manuscript as the modern edition. Liebermann dates the text c. 926–c. 1000, perhaps c. 935.
